edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.population: older adults on long-term opioid therapy
edges.mechanism: Sedation, orthostasis, slowed reaction time, and impaired balance make falls a predictable downstream risk of chronic opioid treatment, especially in older adults.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2019 Yarborough cohort in Pain Med, which ties long-term opioid therapy to falls in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
